title: Continuation invalidation basis: bind the cursor's read-cut to changes that can affect the selected membership or order, not every project write, without weakening project or filter binding; document the exact basis and the restart cost
outcome: Continuation invalidation basis: bind the cursor's read-cut to changes that can affect the selected membership or order, not every project write, without weakening project or filter binding; document the exact basis and the restart cost
acceptance: docs state exactly which changes invalidate a continuation and why; a test shows an unrelated write (a note on an item outside the filtered set) does not invalidate a page while a membership- or order-affecting change does, with the typed refusal unchanged
the refusal text states the reason once, not in both headline and bullet

completion.summary:
Continuations now bind to what can change their pages.
- ls cursors carry a required tagged basis. A listing page has a membership fingerprint over the full filtered sequence and is refused only when membership or order changed, or the clock reversed. Compact next keeps project_cut. A token without a basis is refused.
- Note and observation windows decide by total, boundary and clock. The evaluation window binds (run feed head, item revision).
- A refusal states its reason once.
- Docs and tests show that an unrelated note keeps the page, while a membership or order change refuses with the same typed error.
- Landed as 959767d.
